subject: Inference hosting fit-gap & migration next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + infra discovery (recap + next steps)

Hi Emma — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and a short list of follow-ups so we can recommend the best hosting path for Brightline.

Key points I captured:
- Workloads: real-time conversational triage + nightly batch embeddings for analytics.
- Current stack: primary calls to OpenAI API for NLU, and an internal GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100) used for a small number of latency-sensitive models.
- Compliance: PHI adjacent, must support VPC/isolation for a subset of traffic; SOC2 required; encryption at rest + customer-managed keys preferred.
- Traffic profile: peak concurrent reqs ~120 rps for conversational endpoints; typical seq length 512 tokens; bursty during business hours.
- Migration ask: want a low-risk path off OpenAI for sensitive flows, maintain feature parity, and minimize downtime.

Questions / asks for your team (so we can size and recommend):
1) Which features must run in a private VPC/on-prem vs which can stay on a hosted endpoint? (one-liner mapping is fine)
2) Do you have an internal security contact to run our quick questionnaire (we can share the doc)?
3) Is procurement already involved? I see Tom CC'd — can we confirm target contracting timeline (Q4/Q1)?
4) Any hard latency SLOs for the sensitive path (p95 target)?

Recommended immediate next steps:
- I’ll prepare a short hosting-fit matrix (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) with pros/cons and a suggested phased migration plan. See attachment: redwood-hosting-eval-matrix.xlsx.
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Camila (solutions) and your infra/security (please share 2 windows next week).
- If procurement is ready, we’ll provide a high-level pricing ballpark and draft terms.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the matrix by EOD Wed.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood-hosting-eval-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet - hosting tradeoffs, initial sizing assumptions)

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@brightlinehealth.com>, Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + infra discovery (recap + next steps)

Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap. Answers inline: 

1) Private VPC / isolated path required for PHI-touching flows (triage decisions and any payloads containing health identifiers). Non-PHI conversational features (help center, general routing) can run on a hosted endpoint.
2) Security contact: Tom Keller (cc'd). He can take the questionnaire.
3) Procurement: CC'd (procurement@brightlinehealth.com). Target timeline: evaluate in Oct/Nov, aim to sign pilot by end of Q4.
4) Latency SLO: p95 <= 450ms for the private path; 700ms ok for hosted.

Migration notes: we have an internal team that has been experimenting with containerized LLMs on our A100 cluster for edge cases; we prefer not to expand on-prem ops, but may keep the cluster for low-level experimentation. Primary goal is to consolidate to a managed inference platform that meets our compliance needs and reduces ops overhead.

Please include a cost ballpark for: (a) Hosted API for non-sensitive traffic, (b) Dedicated reserved capacity for the private path, (c) Private on-prem deployment (order of magnitude).

Appreciate the matrix — we’ll review.

—Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Product, Brightline Health
emma.jones@brightlinehealth.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@brightlinehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting fit-gap + phased migration proposal (attached)

Hi Emma / team — following Vanessa's matrix, I pulled together a recommended fit-gap and a phased migration path. High-level summary:

Recommended approach: Hybrid phased rollout
- Phase 0 (Quick win): Use Redwood Hosted API for non-PHI traffic immediately to remove OpenAI dependency for these routes (low lift).
- Phase 1 (Pilot Dedicated): Provision Dedicated reserved capacity with a Private VPC for PHI flows. This gives predictable throughput and isolation while remaining managed by Redwood.
- Phase 2 (Optional On-prem): If any ultra-sensitive workloads must remain on-prem or if policy requires, we can deploy Redwood Private (on-prem bundle) to the cluster — this is higher lift and longer timeline.

Why Dedicated first for PHI:
- Predictable latency and easier autoscaling for peak rps (~120) compared to pure hosted with burst limitations.
- VPC + KMS integrations to meet your CMK preference.
- Can put automatic routing rules so non-PHI stays on Hosted to optimize cost.

Migration plan (very high level):
- Week 0–2: Tech deep dive, collect security questionnaire, confirm VPC/network requirements.
- Week 2–4: Provision Dedicated test pool, run smoke tests with a copy of your traffic (redacted).
- Week 4–8: Pilot cutover for a subset of users, monitoring and quality validation.
- Week 8–12: Ramp to production and de-commission OpenAI for targeted features.

Attachments: milestone-ops-plan.pdf, pricing-estimate.csv (ballpark figures for Hosted / Dedicated / Private).

Notes on migration from OpenAI/self-hosted cluster:
- Tokenization/model parity: we’ll validate prompt outputs and provide regressions checks; minor prompt adjustments expected.
- KV cache and batching: Dedicated gives better unit economics for stable traffic via batching and prefix caching.

Next steps I need from Brightline:
- Confirm security contact availability for questionnaire (Tom),
- Share one representative prompt set for regression checks,
- 2–3 windows for a 45-min deep dive next week.

If procurement wants an itemized draft SOW to plug into your legal review, Aditya can follow up.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Attachments: milestone-ops-plan.pdf (PDF - phased milestones and test criteria), pricing-estimate.csv (CSV - ballpark pricing)

2) Encryption / KMS details and whether customer-managed keys are supported.
3) High-level SOW and ballpark pricing for a 6-month pilot (expected scale: avg 40 rps, peak 120 rps).
4) Template NDA / draft MSAs if available.

Please include any lead times required for Dedicated capacity provisioning and whether Redwood can commit to a pilot SLA for uptime and latency during the evaluation.

Thanks — Tom will coordinate contract review.

2) KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM integrations; details in the attached security brief.
3) SOW / pricing: Attached pricing-estimate.csv and milestone-ops-plan.pdf (6-month pilot option included). Ballpark: Hosted API (non-PHI): ~$0.02/token-equivalent for generation; Dedicated reserved pool (PHI path) estimated monthly committed spend starting at $18k/month for the pilot sizing (we included options in the CSV). Exact numbers tethered to traffic profile and batching.
4) Contracting: we can share a draft MSA/NDA; default lead time for Dedicated pool provisioning is ~5–7 business days after PO, pilot SLA negotiable.

Thanks — forwarding the SOC2 now.
